classification.difficultyReason: Translate tangent slopes into a new graph. The hardest parts require deciding that a horizontal tangent during continued increase gives a derivative zero without a sign change, and using steepness and flattening tails to place the derivative extrema and infer its end behaviour.

content.prompt: The diagrams below show sketches of $y=f(x)$. Copy each diagram into your book. On the same axes, use a different colour to sketch $y=f'(x)$.

spec.description: Blue upward-opening parabola centred on the y-axis with vertex at height 1.
spec.mathematics: Vertex (0,1), both branches extend upward, height 1 is the only numerical label.

answer.short: An increasing straight line through the origin.
answer.worked: The parabola has negative slopes to the left of its vertex and positive slopes to the right. The horizontal tangent is at $x=0$. The slopes of a parabola change at a constant rate, so the derivative is an increasing straight line through the origin.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(a), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(a)
spec.description: Dashed red derivative on the same axes as the blue given parabola.
Blue upward-opening parabola through the origin with a labelled x-axis tick at 2.
spec.mathematics: The vertex lies below the tick at x=2 and below the x-axis. No further numerical labels.

answer.short: An increasing straight line crossing the $x$-axis at $x=2$.
answer.worked: The tangent to the parabola is horizontal at its minimum, where $x=2$. The slopes are negative before this point and positive after it. They increase at a constant rate, giving an increasing straight line through $(2,0)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(b), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(b)
spec.description: Dashed red line crossing the x-axis at the tick labelled 2, on the same axes as the blue parabola.
spec.mathematics: Derivative is an increasing straight line with negative y-intercept.

spec.description: Blue rising cubic-shaped sketch with a maximum left of the origin, a minimum right of it and three crossings of the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: The maximum is above the x-axis, the minimum is below it, and the middle crossing is the origin.

answer.short: An upward-opening parabola crossing the $x$-axis at the two turning-point positions.
answer.worked: The two horizontal tangents give the zeros of $f'$. Reading from left to right, the slopes of $f$ are positive, negative, then positive. The steepest descent is near the $y$-axis, so the derivative has its minimum there, below the $x$-axis.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(c), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(c)
spec.description: Dashed red upward-opening parabola on the axes of the blue cubic-shaped curve.
spec.mathematics: Two derivative zeros align with the two given turning points. The derivative minimum is on the y-axis below the x-axis.

spec.description: Blue asymmetric quartic-shaped sketch with four x-axis crossings and both ends up.
spec.mathematics: Shallower minimum left of the y-axis, small maximum immediately to its right, deeper minimum farther right. The second x-axis crossing is at the origin.

answer.short: A cubic-shaped curve crossing the $x$-axis at all three turning-point positions.
answer.worked: Mark a zero of $f'$ at each of the three horizontal tangents. From left to right, $f$ falls, rises, falls and rises, so $f'$ has signs $-,+,-,+$. Draw its positive hump over the first rising interval and its negative trough over the next falling interval.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(d), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(d)
spec.description: Dashed red cubic-shaped derivative on the given axes.
spec.mathematics: One negative and two positive derivative zeros align with the given turning points, with signs −,+,−,+.

spec.description: Blue falling cubic-shaped sketch with a local minimum at the origin and a positive local maximum to the right.
spec.mathematics: Touches the x-axis at the origin, then crosses at a positive x-value past the maximum.

answer.short: A downward-opening parabola crossing at the origin and at the $x$-coordinate of the given maximum.
answer.worked: The tangent is horizontal at the origin and at the local maximum to its right. The slopes of $f$ are positive between these points and negative on either side, giving a downward-opening parabola crossing at both zeros.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(e), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(e)
spec.description: Dashed red downward-opening parabola on the axes of the given curve.
spec.mathematics: The derivative crosses at the origin and beneath the given maximum.

spec.description: Blue symmetric W-shaped curve with a local maximum at the origin and two minima below the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: The outer x-axis crossings are symmetric. The curve touches the x-axis at its central maximum.

answer.short: A cubic-shaped curve crossing at the origin and at the two given minimum positions.
answer.worked: The three zeros of $f'$ line up with the left minimum, central maximum and right minimum. The graph of $f$ falls, rises, falls and rises. The derivative therefore has signs $-,+,-,+$, with the middle crossing at the origin.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(f), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(f)
spec.description: Dashed red cubic-shaped derivative on the same axes as the symmetric blue curve.
spec.mathematics: Three crossings, with the outer two symmetric and aligned with the given minima.

spec.description: Blue curve with both ends up, a shallow minimum left of the y-axis, and a horizontal tangent at the origin as the curve continues to rise.
spec.mathematics: Crosses the x-axis at a negative x-value and crosses again with a horizontal tangent at the origin. The tangent interpretation is corroborated by R20(g).

answer.short: The derivative crosses the $x$-axis at the given minimum and touches it at the origin.
answer.worked: At the left-hand minimum, $f$ changes from falling to rising, so $f'$ crosses from negative to positive. The tangent is horizontal again at the origin, but $f$ is increasing on both sides. Thus $f'$ touches the $x$-axis at the origin and rises again.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(g), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(g)
spec.description: Dashed red derivative with a negative crossing and a local minimum on the x-axis at the origin.
spec.mathematics: The derivative changes sign at the given minimum and remains positive on both sides of the stationary point at the origin.

spec.description: Blue symmetric valley with a dashed two-ended guide at y=1.
spec.mathematics: The minimum lies on the y-axis below the x-axis. The curve crosses the x-axis on both sides and approaches y=1 from below.
spec.answerVisibility: Given function and its asymptote only.

answer.short: The derivative has a negative trough to the left of the origin and a positive hump to the right. It crosses at the origin and approaches $y=0$ at both ends.
answer.worked: The valley falls to a horizontal tangent at $x=0$ and then rises, so $f'$ is negative on the left, zero at the origin and positive on the right. The steepest descent gives the trough of $f'$ and the steepest rise gives its hump. Both tails of $f$ flatten, so $f'$ approaches zero at both ends.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 20(h), compared with answer PDF 64 R20(h)
spec.description: Dashed red derivative crosses the origin and approaches the x-axis. The black dashed y=1 line belongs to the blue function.
spec.mathematics: Negative left branch and positive right branch, with one extremum in each branch. Both derivative tails approach zero.
